 IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  R/SPECIAL CIVIL APPLICATION NO. 2606 of 2026  ==========================================================
 MAVJIBHAI JIVABHAI NAKUM & ANR.
 Versus  UNION OF INDIA & ORS.
 ==========================================================
 Appearance:
 KAUSHAL H PATEL(9328) for the Petitioner(s) No. 1,2  MR SP MAJMUDAR(3456) for the Petitioner(s) No. 1,2  MR. SANJAY UDHWANI, ASSISTANT GOVERNMENT PLEADER for the  Respondent(s) No. 2,3  MR ANKIT SHAH(6371) for the Respondent(s) No. 1  MR MAULIK G NANAVATI(3318) for the Respondent(s) No. 4,5  ==========================================================

1. The petitioners herein seek a writ in the nature of certiorari for quashing and setting aside the notification dated 09.08.2021 published under Section 3D of the National Highways Act, 1956 (the Act, 1956) as well as the award dated 04.08.2022 passed by the competent authority, NHAI qua the Mavjibhai Jivabhai Nakum vs Union Of India on 3 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13960221/
1 land in question, the description of which has been given in paragraph no. '4' of the writ petition,
Revenue Survey No. 136/1 (Old No. 97 paiki) of Village Harshadpur, Taluka Khambhaliya, District Devbhoomi Dwarka.

sentences.text: 2. The contention in the writ petition is that an area of NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/2606/2026 ORDER DATED: 03/03/2026 undefined 2292 sq. mtrs. of the aforesaid plot has been acquired in the land acquisition proceedings conducted under the National Highways Act, 1956.

It is also an admitted fact that the acquisition proceedings had been brought to its logical end with the making of the award dated 04.08.2022 by the competent authority and the receipt of the compensation by the petitioners.

3. After a period of four years, of receipt of compensation, the petitioners come up in the present petition seeking for quashing of the acquisition proceedings asking for diversiting of the Central Government from the land in question, on the premise that the land in question is not needed by the beneficiary namely the National Highways Authority of India.
4.

It is contended in the writ petition that the petitioners have been informed by the competent authority, NHAI namely the respondent no. 3 herein that the NHAI has intimated that it does not need the land in question and further the petitioners were asked to redeposit the compensation amount.

This assertion is based on a letter dated 21.05.2024, written by the Competent Authority NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/2606/2026 ORDER DATED: 03/03/2026 undefined namely the respondent no. 3 herein appended at page no. '131' of the paper-book.
5.

Mr. Maulik G. Nanavati, learned advocate appearing for the respondent - NHAI has passed on a copy of the communication dated 23.07.2025, sent by the Project Director, NHAI, PIU - Rajkot to the Competent Authority of Land Acquisition, Prant Officer, Khambhalia, District :
Devbhoomi Dwarka for completion of necessary formalities for mutation of the name of Central Government/NHAI in the revenue records with respect to the Revenue Survey No. 136/P, Village Harshadpur and further to handover the physical possession of the land in question to the Project Implementation Unit (PIU), Rajkot.

A perusal of the said communication indicates that the land in question has been acquired for four laning of Dwarka-Khambhaliya-Devariya section from km 203.500 to 176.500 and from km 171.800 to 130.000 of National Highway No. 151A.
6.

The communication dated 23.07.2025 has been sent by the Project Director to the competent authority with reference to its two letters no. NHAI/51/2025 dated 15.05.2025, seeking permission for cancellation of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/2606/2026 ORDER DATED: 03/03/2026 undefined Award passed under Section 3G of the Act, 1956, with respect to the land in question.

It is categorically stated therein that there exists no legal provision under the Act, 1956 for denotification cancellation of the award pertaining to an acquired land, once the same has been notified under Section 3D of the Act, 1956.
The land in question acquired for public purpose, once vests with the Central Government free from all encumbrances, cannot be reverted or denotified at the instance of any landholder.

sentences.text: We may note that under the scheme of the National Highways Act, 1956, with the publication of the notification under Section 3D, by virtue of Section 3D(2) the acquired land vests absolutely in the Central Government free from all encumbrances.
There is no provision for divesting under the Act, 1956.

Moreover, the acquiring body namely the NHAI is empowered to take possession of the acquired land after the same is vested in the Central Government under Section 3D(2) of the Act,
1956 and the compensation amount determined by the competent authority under Section 3G, is deposited in accordance with the provisions of Section 3H(1) of the Act, 1956.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/2606/2026 ORDER DATED: 03/03/2026 undefined 8.

As regards the physical possession of the petitioners over the land in question, suffice it to say that with the vesting of the land in question and disbursement of compensation in accordance with Section 3E (1), the possession of the landholder over the acquired land becomes that of an unauthorised occupation.

Section 3E of the Act, 1956 clearly provides that after the land has vested in the Central Government under Section 3D(2) and the amount determined by the competent authority under Section 3G has been deposited under Section 3H (1), with the competent authority by the Central Government, the competent authority has to issue a notice in writing directing the owner as well as any other person who may be in possession of such land, to surrender or deliver the possession thereof to the competent authority or any person duly authorised by it in this behalf,
within 60 days of the service of notice.

9. It is not the case of the petitioners that no notice whatsoever had been issued by the competent authority under Section 3E (1) after the compensation amount was deposited by the NHAI or disbursed to the petitioners NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/2606/2026 ORDER DATED:
03/03/2026 undefined themselves in the year 2022, itself.
It was otherwise the duty of the competent authority to issue a notice and take the possession of the acquired land.

Instead of conducting such an exercise, the competent authority has illegally indulged in the communications with the petitioners and the NHAI, after a period of two years of conclusion of the land acquisition proceedings.

10. This fact itself makes it evident that the competent authority has acted in collusion with the landholders, permitting them to receive the compensation and also continuing with illegal possession of the acquired land.

The action of the competent authority in writing letters to the petitioners in the year 2024, asking them to redeposit or refund the compensation amount was without any decision or direction of the Central Government, to whom the land in question was vested absolutely by virtue of Section 3D (2).

The Central Government being the owner of the land in question with the vesting of the same by virtue of Section 3D, the competent authority was under obligation to take physical possession and hand over the same to the Central Government as soon as the compensation amount was NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/2606/2026 ORDER DATED:
03/03/2026 undefined deposited with it, in accordance with the Section 3H (1) of the Act, 1956.

11. This is one of such matters, where the State Officer designated as competent authority has indulged in illegal activities at the behest of the landholders who had not only received the compensation much earlier, but also refused to deliver the physical possession of the acquired land.
Mavjibhai Jivabhai Nakum vs Union Of India on 3 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13960221/
3 12.

sentences.text: Taking note of the above, we find that the present petition is wholly misconceived.
The prayers made in the writ petition seeking for quashing of the notification under Section 3D and the award passed under Section 3G(1) of the Act, 1956 cannot be granted.

The writ petition is dismissed,
accordingly.

13. However, for any assertion of the petitioners for redeposit of the compensation amount already paid to them, at the instance of the competent authority, it would be open for the petitioners to file a representation before the Collector, Devbhoomi Dwarka, alongwith the copy of this order.

On receipt of the representation within a period of two weeks from today, it would be incumbent upon the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/2606/2026 ORDER DATED: 03/03/2026 undefined Collector to make an inquiry as to in what circumstances, the officer posted as competent authority, NHAI has indulged in making communication with the petitioners asking them to redeposit or return the compensation amount once disbursed and also made communication with the NHAI dated 15.05.2025 requesting to grant him permission for cancellation of 3G Award.
The Collector shall take decision on the application of the petitioner after conducting the aforesaid inquiry, strictly in accordance with Law.

14. As such the action of the competent authority was wholly beyond its jurisdiction and the Collector is required to make a preliminary inquiry to ascertain the aspect of collusion of the officer posted as competent authority with the petitioners herein.

In case, the Collector reaches at the conclusion that the officer who had indulged in the communication dated 21.05.2024 with the petitioners and the letter No. NHAI/51/2025 dated 15.05.2025 has acted at the behest or in collusion with the petitioners, an appropriate departmental inquiry shall also be initiated against him.

15. This order be served upon the Collector, Devbhoomi NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/2606/2026 ORDER DATED: 03/03/2026 undefined Dwarka by Mr. Sanjay Udhwani, learned Assistant Government Pleader appearing for the State respondents, to initiate necessary action soon after receipt of the copy of this order.
The action taken by the Collector shall be reported to this Court through the Registrar General of the High Court.

16. Further, the Collector, Devbhoomi Dwarka is also required to ensure that the physical possession of the land in question is taken forthwith, and handed over the same to the competent officer of the Project Implementation Unit, Rajkot.
The name of the Central Government/NHAI being the owner of the land in question shall also be required to be mutated in the revenue record, immediately.

17. The proceedings of delivery of possession to the Project Implementation Unit, NHAI, Rajkot with the mutation proceedings is to be completed positively within a period of two weeks from today,
failing which, it would be open for the NHAI to approach this Court again.
(SUNITA AGARWAL, CJ ) (D.N.RAY,J) VARSHA DESAI Mavjibhai Jivabhai Nakum vs Union Of India on 3 March, 2026
